title: Robert Morales and Tiru Chabba — Florida State University shooting
research_notes: Rechecked 2026-10-30. (1) Morales family suit filed. WCTV (2026-08-31) reports that the family of Robert Morales, FSU's dining coordinator, sued OpenAI and Sam Altman in federal court in Tallahassee that Monday (2026-08-31). The complaint runs 53 pages; family attorney Dean LeBoeuf. It alleges OpenAI knew the product was dangerous and should have flagged Ikner's chats in the days, hours and minutes before the shooting. LeBoeuf said settlement talks with OpenAI's lawyers had failed. The Tallahassee Democrat (via Yahoo, 2026-10-05) independently describes a 2026-08-31 suit by Morales's widow. A Justia docket listing, seen only as search-result text because the page blocked automated fetch, shows MORALES v. OPENAI FOUNDATION et al., N.D. Fla. No. 4:26-cv-00425, filed 2026-08-31, plaintiff Betty Morales, counsel Dean Robert LeBoeuf and Ryan Blake Hobbs. Treat the case number and plaintiff name as unverified until the docket is opened. (2) OpenAI moved to dismiss Joshi. On 2026-09-25 OpenAI moved to dismiss Joshi v. OpenAI Foundation (N.D. Fla., Judge Mark Walker), per the Tallahassee Democrat/USA TODAY Network (2026-10-05) and WCTV (2026-09-28). Its arguments: Ikner never told ChatGPT he planned a shooting; the responses were consistently factual and publicly available; ChatGPT refused illegal instructions and referred him to the 988 crisis line when he mentioned depression; information and ideas are not 'products', so a chatbot is no more a defective product than a search engine; there was no special relationship and no duty to prevent a third party's crime; and liability would violate the First Amendment. Plaintiff's counsel Bakari Sellers responded publicly that 'This is not the equivalent of a library.' No ruling found. (3) A second motion. Law360 (2026-10-21, Emily Field, headline 'OpenAI Asserts ChatGPT Not Liable For "Third Party" Crime') reports that OpenAI moved to dismiss three FSU suits in N.D. Fla. on the same theories. The case names are paywalled, so which three suits is not confirmed. (4) Criminal trial delayed. WEAR-TV (2026-08-25) reports that Leon County Circuit Judge Lance Neff, by order of 2026-08-12, moved State v. Ikner from October 2026 to 2027-06-08 and wrote that, absent extraordinary circumstances, no further continuances will be granted. The scout lead's 'pretrial proceedings 2027-05-20' was not found in any source opened. (5) More survivor suits. Reese Gourley (Fasig Brooks; 71-page filing on 2026-08-26) sued OpenAI, per WFSU 2026-08-28. Alianna Grant sued Sam Altman in Leon County Circuit Court around late June 2026, per WCTV 2026-06-30.
case_reference: Civil (wrongful death): Joshi v. OpenAI Foundation et al., No. 4:26-cv-00222-MW-MJF (N.D. Fla., Tallahassee Div., complaint filed 2026-05-10; Judge Mark E. Walker; defendants include eleven OpenAI entities and Phoenix Ikner). OpenAI moved to dismiss on 2026-09-25 (First Amendment; ChatGPT not a 'product'; no duty to prevent a third party's crime); no ruling as of 2026-10-30. Morales family wrongful-death suit against OpenAI and Sam Altman filed 2026-08-31 in N.D. Fla. (Tallahassee), counsel Dean LeBoeuf. A Justia listing, seen only in search results, gives MORALES v. OPENAI FOUNDATION et al., No. 4:26-cv-00425 (plaintiff Betty Morales); unverified. Related survivor suits: Askins v. OpenAI Foundation, No. 4:26-cv-00335, and Mall v. OpenAI Foundation, No. 4:26-cv-00334 (both N.D. Fla., filed 2026-07-14); Reese Gourley v. OpenAI (filed 2026-08-26; Justia listing in search results gives No. 4:26-cv-00416, unverified); Alianna Grant v. Altman (Leon County Circuit Court, around June 2026). Law360 reports a 2026-10-21 OpenAI motion to dismiss three of the FSU suits (case names not confirmed). Criminal: State of Florida v. Phoenix Ikner, Leon County Circuit Court (2nd Judicial Circuit), Judge Lance Neff. Grand jury indictment 2025-05-14 on 2 counts of first-degree murder and 7 counts of attempted first-degree murder; death penalty noticed June 2025. Trial moved by order of 2026-08-12 from 2026-10-19 to 2027-06-08. State case number not located. Regulatory: Florida Attorney General Office of Statewide Prosecution opened a civil probe on 2026-04-09 and escalated it to a criminal investigation of OpenAI on 2026-04-21, with subpoenas.
counterevidence:
OpenAI denies causation on the record: 'Last year's mass shooting at Florida State University was a tragedy, but ChatGPT is not responsible for this terrible crime. In this case, ChatGPT provided factual responses to questions with information that could be found broadly across public sources on the internet, and it did not encourage or promote illegal or harmful activity.' It also says that after learning of the shooting it identified an account believed to be the suspect's, proactively gave that to law enforcement, and cooperated. The public-availability defense is not trivial for several of the quoted outputs (media-coverage thresholds, building foot traffic), even if their aggregation is damning in context.

OpenAI's 2026-09-25 motion to dismiss in Joshi, as reported by the Tallahassee Democrat and WCTV, sharpens this. It argues that Ikner never told ChatGPT he was planning or intended to commit a shooting. It argues that the responses were 'consistently factual', that ChatGPT refused illegal instructions and never encouraged violence, and that it encouraged him to seek help and referred him to the 988 crisis line when he mentioned depression. It adds that information and ideas are not 'products' (comparing ChatGPT to a search engine), that Florida imposes no duty to prevent a third party's crime absent a special relationship or knowledge of a specific threat, and that liability would violate the First Amendment. A similar motion against three further FSU suits followed on 2026-10-21 (Law360). These are advocacy positions in an unruled motion, not findings.

Competing causes are substantial and, unlike the AI thread, are the subject of a pending criminal prosecution. Ikner obtained his stepmother's former service weapon, had a long-documented ideological and grievance trajectory, and is himself a named defendant in the civil case. The complaint's own theory is largely about failure to flag or escalate: ChatGPT did not refuse or escalate. It does not prove that any single output caused the attack. Two internal inconsistencies weaken the pleading as evidence. Para. 163 refers to 'the day before the shooting, April 26, 2025', which does not match the 2025-04-17 shooting date. And sources give the end of the AG subpoena window as both 2025-04-17 and '2026'. Finally, the criminal trial has not happened (now set for 2027-06-08), so no fact-finder has tested any of it.

title: Joshua Enneking, 26
research_notes: Rechecked 2026-10-30. No Enneking-specific ruling, answer, demurrer or settlement found in JCCP 5431. A secondary tracker (openclassactions.com, updated 2026-10-27) says, without a primary source, that discovery opened in late September 2026 and that OpenAI's first responses to the coordinated complaints were due 2026-10-30; neither claim is verified. The related Florida AG enforcement action has moved. OpenAI removed it from Highlands County Circuit Court to the S.D. Fla. (Fort Pierce, Judge Aileen Cannon), citing COPPA, and Florida moved to remand on 2026-07-10 (WQCS, 2026-07-13). Mealey's (2026-09-10) reports that a federal judge in Fort Pierce sent the case back to state court for lack of jurisdiction over the state consumer-protection claims. The ABA Journal (2026-09-30) reports that the AG then asked Judge Heather Beato of Florida's 10th Judicial Circuit for a temporary injunction barring OpenAI from developing new models without independent oversight. None of these reports mentions Enneking specifically.
case_reference: Karen Enneking, individually and as successor-in-interest to Decedent Joshua Enneking v. OpenAI, Inc., OpenAI OpCo, LLC, OpenAI Holdings, LLC, and Samuel Altman, Superior Court of California, County of San Francisco, Case No. CGC-25-630809, filed 2025-11-06. Coordinated into Judicial Council Coordination Proceeding No. 5431, In re: ChatGPT Product Liability Cases (SF Superior Court, Judge Schulman); coordination order dated 2026-02-03; Case Management Order No. 1, entered 2026-08-04, established plaintiffs' leadership. No ruling on the merits as of 2026-10-30. Related state enforcement action: State of Florida ex rel. Attorney General James Uthmeier v. OpenAI and Samuel Altman, filed in Highlands County Circuit Court (10th Judicial Circuit) on 2026-06-01, which publicly highlights Joshua Enneking's death. OpenAI removed it to S.D. Fla. (Fort Pierce, Judge Aileen Cannon), and it was remanded to state court around September 2026. Now before Judge Heather Beato; the AG moved for a temporary injunction on about 2026-09-29. Case number not located. No criminal case.
